subject: Chemistry
title: Primary & Secondary Batteries (Lead Storage & Mercury Cell)
topics: Primary Batteries: Dry Cell (1.5 V) vs Mercury Cell (1.35 V constant voltage because zero dissolved ions in overall reaction)
Secondary Batteries: Lead Storage Battery (Discharging/Recharging chemistry, H₂SO₄ density changes)
Hydrogen-Oxygen (H₂-O₂) Fuel Cells (High 70% efficiency, pure condensed water product)
quickSummary: Primary: Non-rechargeable. Mercury cell delivers constant 1.35 V (no dissolved ions in reaction). Lead storage battery (secondary): Discharging produces PbSO₄ and consumes H₂SO₄ (density drops from 1.30 g/mL); recharging reverses this. H₂-O₂ fuel cells have 70% efficiency.
summary: Master commercial battery chemistry, discharging/recharging reactions, and fuel cell operating mechanics.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Primary Batteries: Dry Cell vs. Mercury Cell
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Primary Batteries: Dry Cell vs. Mercury Cell

summaryBox.title: Mercury Cell Constant Voltage
summaryBox.takeaway: Overall: Zn(Hg) + HgO(s) ──► ZnO(s) + Hg(l). Contains ZERO dissolved ions, so potential remains strictly 1.35 V throughout its life.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MERCURY CELL CHEMISTRY

• Anode:   Zn-Hg Amalgam
• Cathode: Paste of HgO + C
• Electrolyte: Moist paste of KOH + ZnO
• Net Reaction: Zn(Hg) + HgO(s) ──► ZnO(s) + Hg(l)  (E_cell = 1.35 V CONSTANT!)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Dry Cell / Leclanché ($1.5\text{ V}$)**: Zinc anode, Carbon cathode with $\text{MnO}_2/\text{C}$, $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}/\text{ZnCl}_2$ electrolyte.
• **Mercury Cell ($1.35\text{ V}$)**: The overall cell reaction involves only solid and liquid pure substances with **zero dissolved ions**, providing a constant $1.35\text{ V}$ output.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.2 Lead Storage Battery & H₂-O₂ Fuel Cells
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Lead Storage Battery & H₂-O₂ Fuel Cells
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
LEAD STORAGE BATTERY DISCHARGING

• Anode:   Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) ──► PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻
• Cathode: PbO₂(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) + 4H⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ ──► PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l)
• Net:     Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 2H₂SO₄(aq) ──► 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l)
  (H₂SO₄ consumed ⟹ Electrolyte density DECREASES! Recharging regenerates H₂SO₄)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Lead Storage Battery**: Discharging consumes $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, dropping density from $1.30\text{ g/mL}$; recharging reverses the reaction.
• **$\text{H}_2\text{-O}_2$ Fuel Cell**: Converts fuel combustion directly into electrical energy with $\mathbf{\approx 70\%\ \text{efficiency}}$, producing pure $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

quickRevision: Mercury cell voltage stays constant at 1.35 V (no dissolved ions).
Lead storage battery: Discharging consumes H₂SO₄ (density drops).
Recharging lead battery deposits Pb at anode and PbO₂ at cathode.
